title: Micro-dropin framing: transient quality regressions — quick Q&A + talking points (scratch)
content:
Context:
- Quick founder drop-in (10 minutes) with product + ops today at 10:30am PT. Audience: ~40 engineers + PMs + SREs; purpose: 1) acknowledge customer-reported quality dip, 2) reassure about scope and remediation, 3) align org on customer messaging and next steps.
- Short version: a quantization rollout (opt-q4) triggered unexpected tokenization edgecases for a small subset of long-context chat sessions; we've rolled back the _rollout_ to baseline 1.7 for affected traffic and are running canary tests.
- Why this draft: want a tight 90s opening + 6 Q&A snippets. Keep it founder-forward (empathy, ownership, specificity), avoid technical deep-dives in the drop-in (point to followup channel/doc).

Quick opening (90s script) — use with slight improv: 
"Thanks — quick update. We saw a transient regression in output quality after a quantization change hit a fraction of chat sessions last night. No data breach, no customer data was exposed, and throughput/latency were not impacted. We rolled back the change for affected traffic, put the previous baseline back in, and are running focused canaries while the applied ML team completes root-cause analysis. We own this — I know every minute you spend debugging matters; thank you. We have a short plan for customers and an internal checklist to reduce recurrence. We'll follow up with a written incident summary by EOD tomorrow."

One-sentence goal for drop-in: restore clarity and calm, set timeline, and assign single-threaded follow-ups (owner + ETA).

Top-line bullets to call out (do not read verbatim — use as anchors):
- What happened: quantization profile opt-q4 produced subtle tokenization misalignments for long-prompt cases (approx 0.6% of active sessions) — manifested as hallucinated list items and truncated answers.
- Impact: small percentage of customers; no SLA breaches; no customer data exposure.
- Immediate mitigation: rolled back rollout to baseline model for affected traffic, paused further opt-q4 deployment, enabled extra canary instrumentation (sampling + human review).
- Next steps: deep RCA led by applied-ml (Mikaela) + model infra (Rowan); completion target 72 hours; public-facing postmortem + remediation plan within 5 business days.
- Customer comms: targeted outreach for customers who hit the failure pattern; a short safe-message for general users (ops will draft).

Expected Qs + suggested answers (concise):
Q: How many customers were affected?
A: Preliminary signal shows ~0.6% of chat sessions experienced quality issues; we’re correlating with customer IDs now. Exact customer list + timeline will be in the postmortem. (Owner: Rowan; ETA: EOD)

Q: Was any PII or customer data lost or exposed?
A: No evidence of data exposure. This was a model behavior/quality regression, not a security event. We’ve logged and retained the relevant requests for investigation under KMS-backed storage. (Owner: Security contact TBD — add Sonia?)

Q: Why did the quantized variant degrade quality?
A: Early hypothesis: small changes in floating-point handling for certain attention kernels changed token probabilities in long contexts; we’re reproducing locally and running controlled A/B tests to validate. This is technical — we’ll publish a technical appendix in the RCA. (Owner: Mikaela)

Q: Can we still ship other planned improvements?
A: We’ve paused opt-q4 rollout. Non-related low-risk infra fixes continue. For model-touch changes, we’ll require an expanded canary (longer sequences + human eval) until we close this RCA.

Q: Will customers need to do anything?
A: No action required; we’ve rolled back the change for affected traffic. We’ll proactively contact customers who saw degraded outputs.

Q: How are we preventing recurrence?
A: Short-term: expanded canaries and human eval gates; medium-term: add long-context suite to our Optimize regression harness and improve kernel-level fuzz tests. We also plan to update rollout checklists.

Quick facts / numbers to have on hand (note: confirm before drop-in)
- Initial signal time: 2026-03-11 22:14 PT (on-call alert threshold tripped)
- Rollout window for opt-q4: 2026-03-11 21:30–22:05 PT (partial)
- Estimated affected sessions: ~0.6% of chat sessions (sampled); ~1200 sessions in last 24h matching failure pattern (TBD)
- Customer-reported tickets so far: 4 open (CS triage)

Escalation & single-threaded ownership (for drop-in):
- Technical RCA lead: Mikaela Ruiz (applied-ml)
- Infra + rollback owner: Rowan Lee (serving-runtime)
- Customer comms + CS lead: Maya K. (CS) — note: reach out to Maya in Slack now
- Security liaison: Sonia Patel (security) — flag for audit/retention confirmation

Immediate action items (scratchy):
- [ ] Confirm customer list and send targeted outreach template (Owner: Maya; ETA: 4 hours)
- [ ] Lock canary config and increase human eval sampling (Owner: Rowan; ETA: 2 hours)
- [ ] Run controlled reproduce with full-precision vs opt-q4 on known failure traces (Owner: Mikaela; ETA: 24h)
- [ ] Draft short user-safe message for status.redwood.ai + in-product banner (Owner: Ops comms; ETA: 6 hours)
- [ ] Add long-context tests to Optimize harness backlog (Owner: Optimize PM; ETA: sprint planning)

Notes to self (voicey, do not read aloud):
- Keep the framing: "transient quality regression" (not "bug" or "model failure" in opening) — preserves neutral tone.
- Avoid jitter: focus on single timeline + owners. Don’t promise dates unless owners OK.
- If asked about money/credits: defer to finance/CS; default: targeted credits for deeply impacted enterprise customers after review.
- Legal should review any wording that implies liability — run customer-facing templates by Leah in Legal if we escalate.

Routing / follow-up doc links to paste in drop-in chat:
- RCA tracker (new): confluence/pages/INF-qa-dropin-2026
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-4892
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/long-context-canary

Micro close (two lines for the founder):
"We fixed the immediate impact by rolling back the rollout, we have a clear single-threaded investigation owner, and we’ll publish a postmortem with remediation and timeline. Thanks to ops and applied-ml for the quick triage — we’ll keep everyone posted."

Lingering questions / TBDs (for follow up):
- Confirm security owner for evidence retention (Sonia?)
- Decide whether to issue a short status page note vs. waiting for targeted outreach
- Final decision on customer credits threshold (CS + Finance)

-- end scratchpad --
(Reasonable to hand to Mikaela + Rowan to tighten language before drop-in. Keep this doc internal-only.)
